subject: SDK signal: prefetch timeout + retry surface — urgent field ask
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Walters <ops@avasystems.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDK signal: prefetch timeout + retry surface — urgent field ask

Hi Soojin / Karthik —

Quick summary: Ava Systems (deal blurb below) is hitting intermittent production failures where a prefetch call in their SDK times out and the client retries in a way that causes an expanded tail latency profile and some token duplication in downstream logs. They are in a POC and we need a field-grade mitigation + guidance for their engineers while we consider a longer runtime fix.

What I'm asking:
- Can the runtime team expose an "early-defer" signal or a deterministic 429-style error for prefetch requests that exceed X ms so SDKs can switch to a soft-fallback path?
- Short-term: can we provide an SDK-side recommended retry jitter/backoff config and a documented heuristic to avoid duplicate token emission?

Customer impact:
- Related account: Ava Systems (POC, potential $/yr if they convert)
- Observed: spike in request latencies at 95/99, occasional duplicate completions that break their downstream idempotency checks.
- Attached: abbreviated logs and a prefetched KV trace they shared.

Notes / constraints:
- They are on a dedicated pool in us-west with burst capacity; this looks like prefix prefetch saturation rather than model overload.
- They are sensitive to any behavior that might change semantics of generation (cannot drop tokens) — so a graceful switch to a fallback model/variant is preferable to truncation.

Can the runtime team advise whether an explicit prefetch timeout signal is feasible in the next 2 weeks, and if not, what the recommended SDK mitigation is? If possible, we need a short set of copyable lines for me to send to their eng team today.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: avasystems-logs-2026-05-16.txt, prefetch-trace-annotated.zip
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Walters <ops@avasystems.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK signal: prefetch timeout + retry surface — urgent field ask

Hey team —

Thanks for the signal and the logs, Marissa. I had a quick look through the attached prefetched KV trace. A few quick observations:

- We see long tail latencies clustered around prefetching the final token windows — likely due to concurrent KV cache writes + a small windowed GC activity on that node.
- The client retry pattern from the logs is aggressive: 3 immediate retries with minimal jitter. That explains the amplification.

Feasibility notes:
- Exposing an explicit runtime-level "prefetch timeout" indicator is doable, but not without a short flag + rollout. We can implement an internal metric and a 429-like soft signal for prefetch requests; ETA ~3 weeks for a safe canary (needs kernel selection unit tests to avoid regressions).
- Short-term mitigation we can recommend to SDK: exponential backoff with jitter starting at 50ms, cap at 800ms, and a per-request idempotency token to dedupe completions on the client side (we can give a snippet). This will prevent the immediate amplification while preserving semantics.

Proposed immediate reply to customer (copyable):
"Ben — we've identified a hot window causing prefetch latency amplification. For now please update your SDK to enable exponential backoff with jitter (initial 50ms, max 800ms) and include a per-prefetch idempotency token. We'll follow up with a runtime signal you can opt into for definitive soft-429 responses in ~3 weeks."

I'll follow up with a concise SDK snippet. Tagging Soojin for runtime validation and Lauren for PM prioritization.

- Karthik

(On file: INF-2847 created for the runtime signal work.)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Walters <ops@avasystems.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK signal: prefetch timeout + retry surface — urgent field ask

Appreciate the quick triage.

Operational clarifications from runtime side:

- Implementation approach: we plan to add a prefetch soft-failure code (X-Prefetch-Status: DEGRADED) and a corresponding metric. That will be behind a feature flag so we can opt specific customers into canary.
- Risk: if clients interpret the signal as a final failure and drop requests, we can cause functional regressions. We need the SDK teams to implement the soft-fallback path as Marissa requested (switch to a smaller variant or reduce sequence window) rather than abort.

Timeline and next steps:
1) INF-2847 assigned to runtime sprint — initial canary planned in 3 weeks.
2) Soojin to produce a short spec + header semantics doc for SDK consumption by EOD Wednesday.
3) Marissa to pilot the SDK mitigations with Ava Systems and report back logs.

Marissa — I attached a short annotated trace (prefetch-trace-annotated.zip) with the exact request ids that show the amplification windows. If you can run the suggested SDK change this afternoon we can validate the behavior before the canary.

Soojin
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Walters <ops@avasystems.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK signal: prefetch timeout + retry surface — urgent field ask

Ben —

Thanks for the quick context call earlier. Based on the runtime recommendation please try the following change in your SDK today (minimal patch):

1) Add per-prefetch idempotency token (UUID) on the request. Store the last-seen token server-side for 1 minute and dedupe completions.
2) Enable exponential backoff with jitter: initial_delay=50ms, multiplier=2, max_delay=800ms, max_retries=4.
3) If you receive an X-Prefetch-Status: DEGRADED header, switch to the small-variant fallback model for this request instead of aborting.

I've attached the small log snippet from your environment that maps to the request ids in the annotated trace. Can you push the change to your staging channel and send results by EOD tomorrow? We will plan the runtime canary in 3 weeks but want to validate these SDK mitigations first.

If this works we'll convert the INF-2847 ticket to a prioritized runtime story and propose a limited canary flag for Ava Systems in the next release.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: avasystems-logs-2026-05-16.txt (excerpt)
